Referring to Figure Q.1:
- **Circuit Components:** A sinusoidal input $v_i$ with peak $+10\text{ V}$ and $-10\text{ V}$, a series resistor ($10\text{ k}\Omega$), two parallel branches with Silicon ($Si$) diodes in opposite directions connected to DC reference voltages ($5.3\text{ V}$ and $7.3\text{ V}$). 
- **Diode Forward Voltage Drop:** $V_D = 0.7\text{ V}$ for Silicon.
- **Analysis of Positive Half-Cycle:**
  - As $v_i$ increases positively, the right diode branch conducts when the voltage across it exceeds $7.3\text{ V} + 0.7\text{ V} = 8.0\text{ V}$.
  - Thus, the output voltage $v_o$ is clipped at $+8.0\text{ V}.
- **Analysis of Negative Half-Cycle:**
  - As $v_i$ goes negative, the left diode branch conducts when the voltage exceeds $5.3\text{ V} + 0.7\text{ V} = 6.0\text{ V}$ in the negative direction.
  - Thus, the output voltage $v_o$ is clipped at $-6.0\text{ V}.
- **Output Waveform:** A sine wave clipped symmetrically/asymmetrically at upper limit $+8\text{ V}$ and lower limit $-6\text{ V}$.
proTip: Always add the diode barrier potential ($0.7\text{ V}$ for Si) to the DC reference voltage source to find the exact clipping threshold.
